Subject: Packaging questions — tier posture & burst needs

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile, but procurement and architecture have a few open questions before we move forward:

- We currently use a mix of reserved capacity and on-demand for inference. Curious which Redwood packaging you’d recommend for predictable throughput with occasional burst month-over-month.
- Can we mix a smaller dedicated pool for our critical pipelines and a metered host plan for lower-priority traffic without losing the same API interface?
- Pricing ask: what discounts are typical for a 12–18 month commitment? Any levers (credits, seat bundling, feature gates) we should consider to hit our 20% unit-cost target?

We’re aiming for procurement sign-off by the end of April. Can you share a quick note of options (upgrade/downgrade paths + tradeoffs) and attach any SOW-ish template you’d use? I can loop in procurement (procurement@claritymed.com) if helpful.

Best,

Procurement Manager, ClarityMed

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. I’ve attached a short options sheet (Proposed_Tier_Options.pdf) and a draft SOW so procurement has something to review. High-level summary below:

1) Recommended packaging mix (for your usage profile)
   - Primary: Dedicated pool (small) for critical inference pipelines. Guarantees throughput + SLA.
   - Secondary: Hosted (metered) for background/experimentation traffic. Same API surface and routing; we handle the routing fallback policy.

2) Burst model
   - Option A: Dedicated with burst credits (pre-purchased token credits usable during spikes) — predictable invoice and easier cost modeling.
   - Option B: Autoscale on Dedicated with capped burst (higher unit cost during burst) — simpler but slightly more expensive.

3) Discounts / levers
   - 12–18 month commit typically yields 10–20% off hosted unit rates plus credits.
   - Bundling seats + reserved capacity -> additional negotiation room (seat-level discounts and onboarding credits).
   - Proration and step-down guardrails: we can offer a graded downgrade path to protect your spend targets.

Next steps: can we do a 30-min call tomorrow (Thu 3/23) to walk the options and let me loop in Ben (solutions) and Lauren (pricing/ops) if that works? If you prefer I’ll send a redlineable SOW now.

Attachments: Proposed_Tier_Options.pdf, SOW-draft-ClarityMed.docx

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer

Karthik — quick technical recs for ClarityMed:

- Dedicated pool: 2x A10G-equivalent nodes to start (redundant pair) with 16k context support. That covers steady critical pipelines and keeps latency in single-digit 100ms range for your models.
- Quantization: recommend int8 quant for lower-priority models to reduce token cost ~2.5x; keep FP16 for latency-sensitive pipelines.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for their most common prompts; we’ll need a short prompt corpus to estimate hit rate but this typically reduces tokens by ~30%.
- Burst approach: go with Dedicated + pre-purchased burst credits (Option A). Allows predictable cost modeling for procurement and avoids spike throttling during big events.

I’ll add a short sizing note to the Proposed_Tier_Options.pdf. From a product POV, mixing dedicated + hosted is supported natively — no SDK changes.

— Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Karthik / Ben — pricing/opinion from ops:

- For a 12-month commit we can offer a 12% blended discount on hosted unit rates + $15k onboarding credit (applied to the first 60 days).
- For an 18-month commit we can move to 18% blended discount + $25k onboarding credit + 10% off burst credits.
- Seat bundling: if they commit to a minimum of 5 seat licenses for SRE/Analytics we can add a one-time migration/enablement credit of $7,500.
- Proration & downgrade: we’ll allow a single step-down at 9 months with a 60-day notice and graded step (no penalty if usage midpoint <= 75% of committed).

I’ve uploaded a pricing snapshot in HubSpot and added suggested SOW language for the downgrade guardrail. See link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/CLMD-2028-Q1-07

If they push for deeper discount we should ask for a longer commit or increase the reserved capacity portion (higher committed spend gives more concession room).

— Lauren
Sales Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
